Challenging judgment and award dated 09.06.2014 passed by Additional District and Sessions Judge at Gadag, ('Tribunal' for short) in MVC no.134/2008, this appeal is filed.

entities.text: Additional District and Sessions Judge at Gadag
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. Sri Ramachandra V. Bhat learned counsel appearing for Sri FV Patil, advocate for appellant submitted that, appeal was by owner of vehicle challenging finding in award on liability.

It was submitted, in a claim petition filed by respondent no.1 herein, it was stated that on 14.08.2006,
when claimant was proceeding on a motorcycle with his friend, driver of Tata Indica Car no.KA-35/10476 NT drove it in rash and negligent manner and dashed against motorcycle causing incident.
In said accident, claimant sustained grievous injuries and despite treatment did not recover fully and sustained loss of earning capacity.
Claiming compensation, he filed claim petition under Section 166 of MV Act against owner and insurer of car.

3. In claim petition, a contention was urged by insurer that temporary registration of vehicle had expired and vehicle was not registered as on date of accident and therefore, insurer could not be made liable.

Addressing said contentions, Tribunal NC: 2026:KHC-D:3547 HC-KAR relying on two judgments of this Court held for want of registration and expiry of temporary registration, question of calling upon insurer to indemnify owner would not arise and had dismissed claim petition against Premanath S/O. sentences.text: On said ground sought for allowing appeal.
4. On other hand, Sri NR Kuppelur learned counsel for respondent-insurer opposed appeal.
It was submitted that plying motor vehicle without registration would be a fundamental breach of terms and conditions of policy and in violation of Section 39 of Motor Vehicles Act 1988.

Besides Hon'ble Supreme Court in case of Narinder Singe V. New India Assurance Company Limited and others2 had confirmed an award passed by National Consumer Dispute Redressal Commission rejecting a consumer complaint, claiming compensation from insurer, in 2016:KHC-K:1303 Civil Appeal No.8463/2014 arising out of SLP (Civil) no.26308/2013 NC: 2026:KHC-D:3547 HC-KAR respect of a motor vehicle accident on ground that, temporary registration of vehicle had expired and vehicle was not registered at time of accident.
5.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In view of decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court, contention of appellant would not be tenable

,
consequently, appeal is dismissed.

6. Amount in deposit is ordered to be transmitted to Tribunal for payment.

opennyai_summary.arguments:
It was submitted that said reasoning was not tenable in view of decision of this Court in case of Branch Manager, National Insurance Company Limited V. Shaik Omar and others1, wherein it was held mere non registration of vehicle would not be a ground for exoneration of insurance company.

opennyai_summary.decision:
On said ground sought for allowing appeal.

,
consequently, appeal is dismissed.
